translations.text: For hell will not praise you, nor will death praise you, nor will those who go down into the pit wait for your truth. The living, the living himself will praise you, as I do today; the father will make your truth known to the children. Lord, save me, and we will sing our psalms all the days of our life in the house of the Lord.

My heart has rejoiced in the Lord, and my horn is lifted up in my God; my mouth is opened wide over my enemies, for I have rejoiced in your salvation. There is no one holy as the Lord is; indeed there is no other besides you, and there is no one stronger than our God. Do not [?]

[?] she who had children was made weak. The Lord puts to death and makes alive; he leads down to hell and leads back again. The Lord makes poor and makes rich; he humbles and lifts up. He raises the wretched from the dust and

lifts the poor up from the dung, so that he may sit with princes and hold a throne of glory. For the hinges of the earth are the Lord's, and he set the world upon them. He will guard the feet of his saints, and the wicked will fall silent in darkness.

For no man will be made strong by his own strength. His adversaries will fear the Lord; he will thunder over them in heaven. The Lord will judge the ends of the earth, and he will give power to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed.

and there will be no herd in the stalls. But I will rejoice in the Lord, and I will be glad in God my Savior. God the Lord is my strength, and he will make my feet like those of harts, and he, the victor, will lead me out upon my high places, singing in praises.

Hear, O heavens, what I speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth. Let my teaching grow like rain; let my speech flow like dew, as upon the grass, and like drops upon the grain. For I will call upon the name of the Lord: give greatness to our God. God's works are perfect, and all his ways are judgments. God is faithful and without any un[?]

When the Most High divided the nations, when he separated the children of Adam, he set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel. But the Lord's portion is his [?] people, Jacob the cord of his inheritance. He found

him in a desert land, in a place of horror and of wilderness. He led him about and taught him and guarded him as the apple of his eye. Like an eagle watching over its young to make them fly, and over them
spreads its wings, and takes them up and carries them on its shoulders, the Lord alone was his leader, and there was no foreign god with him. He set him upon high [?]
